authoredSolutions.35: In o-nitrophenol the \(-OH\) and \(-NO_{2}\) groups are close enough to form an intramolecular hydrogen bond (chelation), which locks the molecule up and prevents intermolecular association; the molecules are therefore only weakly held together and the compound is steam volatile, so Statement I is true. That same chelation means o-nitrophenol has little intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so its melting point (about \(45^{\circ}C\)) is much lower than that of the para isomer (about \(114^{\circ}C\)), which is intermolecularly hydrogen bonded. Statement II therefore states the opposite of the fact and is false, giving option (D).
authoredSolutions.36: In the Hinsberg test a primary amine gives a sulphonamide that still carries an \(N-H\), which is acidic because of the two adjacent sulphonyl oxygens, so it dissolves in alkali; a secondary amine gives a sulphonamide with no \(N-H\) and is therefore insoluble in alkali. The product being alkali-insoluble fixes the amine as secondary, which rules out ethylamine. Ammonolysis of ethyl chloride, \(C_{2}H_{5}Cl + NH_{3}\), can only build amines whose alkyl groups are ethyl, so the amine is the secondary ethyl amine, i.e. diethylamine. Among the choices only option (A) is a secondary amine bearing an \(N\)-ethyl group, so (A) is correct.

authoredSolutions.81:
Substitute \(u=x-1\), so the curve becomes \(y=\big||u|-2\big|\); the answer is the same because a horizontal shift does not change area.

Find where the curve meets \(y=2\): \(\big||u|-2\big|=2\Rightarrow |u|-2=\pm 2\Rightarrow |u|=4\) or \(|u|=0\). So the line touches the curve at \(u=-4,\ 0,\ 4\).

On \([0,4]\): for \(0\le u\le 2\), \(y=2-u\); for \(2\le u\le 4\), \(y=u-2\). The curve dips to \(y=0\) at \(u=2\) and rises back to \(y=2\) at \(u=4\). By symmetry the shape on \([-4,0]\) is the mirror image, so the required area is
\[\text{Area}=2\int_{0}^{4}\big(2-y\big)\,du.\]

Compute the two pieces:
\[\int_{0}^{2}\big(2-(2-u)\big)\,du=\int_{0}^{2}u\,du=2,\qquad \int_{2}^{4}\big(2-(u-2)\big)\,du=\int_{2}^{4}(4-u)\,du=\Big[4u-\tfrac{u^{2}}{2}\Big]_{2}^{4}=8-6=2.\]

Thus \(\int_{0}^{4}(2-y)\,du=2+2=4\), and the total area \(=2\times 4=8.\)
